requirements_summary: Customer building agent-assist that must cite support knowledge (ticket history, KB, docs). Needs multi-source retrieval with line-level citations, freshness guarantees for recent tickets, and tool-calling to create/update tickets. Latency SLOs: sub-150ms median for agent UI and 99th percentile under 400ms for typical queries; must gracefully handle burst spikes (target 5k rps burst capacity). Data residency + KMS required for EU customers. Prefer dedicated capacity or private deployment for predictable throughput and isolation.
notes: POC goals: 1) relevance + citation quality vs baseline, 2) 99th pct latency under spike, 3) seamless tool-calling auth model
Client pain: agents waste 20-40% time context-switching, duplicate replies, poor freshness for last-24h tickets
RAG specifics discussed: hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense), per-source TTL, provenance lines + anchor text for attachments
Quote (Nina, CTO): 'We need answers that link back to the original ticket line — not a hallucinated paraphrase.'
Tool-calling flows: create-ticket, escalate-to-L2, append-suggested-canned-response, close-ticket via service account. Must support scoped OAuth and audit log entries per action.
Security: legal asked for data residency mapping for EU customers and proof of customer-managed KMS integration (HSM optional). SOC2 report and penetration test summary requested.
Ops ask: show autoscale behavior under simulated holiday spikes; prefer Dedicated GPU pools with burst capacity and deterministic tail latency.
Tech constraints: existing infra uses Postgres for metadata, S3 for attachments, Confluence for KB; want connectors + incremental ingest (near-real-time) not nightly only.
Success metrics for POC: RAG precision@3 >= 0.78, citation accuracy >= 95%, end-to-end mean latency <= 120ms for agent queries, tool-call roundtrip <= 300ms, support cost reduction estimate >= 15%
